items.title: 67802_Charles Mingus oral history interview
items.q: Mark Williams hears about it, Nat Hentoff tells him, then he'll talk to us about it.

ctx.x: a five-four or a three-four, there should be an accent on one of the beats, similar to the four-four. So on the three-four, it'd be one Two three, one TWO three, one TWO three. And then I said, well, what's wrong with jazz? Well, the guys -- their knowledge is not -- their education has not encompassed classical music. They don't realize that sometimes basses hold notes for five minutes, on one note, pedal point. Or so close to that one note that it's just a variation of that one chord. while the rest of the…

So I said, "Well, (unintelligible) says, 'I'm going to bring that in, I'm going to do it like on Tijuana (unintelligible). That's Table Dance' 'Blue Cae' and another one called Celia,' utilize a pedal point chord. I'm doing it as a half-note and Mark Williams hears about it, Nat Hentoff tells him, then he'll talk to us about it. Comes back and says, And he brings me a sheet 'Hey, man, you know Jelly Roll did that? (Unintelligible) see the paper. I said, 'Well, that's fine, man, but I'm doing it now.' I said, 'I…

So I keep on doing that, and -- with the guys still playing 'Bebop,' (singing), oh, shit, I'm tired of this bullshit. So Charlie Parker he probably didn't play like that, anyway. So I stick to my stuff, it's five years later, Miles Davis is cussing me out for playing one chord. He's doing the same thing, even worse. He but his elbow on the piano, with no tone-sound. tonal center. Most of the things I do, it always has some tonal center. Maybe (unintelligible) a 1/2 step a tonal center. apart, but there's…
